newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil spill no threat to Japan Sea reactors - utility.
newsitem.headline: Oil spill no threat to Japan Sea reactors - utility.

text.p: Nuclear reactors along the Sea of Japan coast will operate normally even if slicks from an oil spill enter their intake pipes, a spokesman for Kansai Electric Power Co Inc said on Thursday.
"The clumps of oil which are near our nuclear plants are small and will not affect the operations even if they enter the intake pipes," he said.
"We are not worried about the oil spill hindering power generation from our reactors," he said.
Kansai Electric operates three nuclear power plants -- Ohi, Takahama and Mihama -- along the Sea of Japan coast.
The three plants comprise 11 pressurised water reactors with combined total capacity of 9.8 million kilowatts.
Six rows of oil fences have been erected to protect the 15 nuclear reactors scattered around Wakasa Bay, the world's highest concentration of nuclear power plants.
"It is possible some oil may have passed the ring of oil fences, however, chances of oil actually entering the intake pipe are slim," The Kansai Electric spokesman said.
He said the mouth of the intake pipe is about seven to eight meters below water, and that the clumps of oil were floating on the surface.
The four other nuclear reactors around the Wakasa Bay owned by the Japan Atomic Power Co, and The Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp are closed for maintenence checks or repairs.
